hero.subtitle: Enabling full-duplex, bidirectional communication over a single TCP connection, powering real-time web applications from chat to live data.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
WebSocket provides a full-duplex communication channel over a single TCP connection. Unlike HTTP's request-response model, WebSocket allows both client and server to send messages independently at any time.

Before WebSocket, real-time web apps relied on inefficient techniques like long-polling, Server-Sent Events, or Comet. WebSocket provides a clean, efficient solution for bidirectional communication.

sections.title: Opening Handshake
sections.content:
WebSocket connections start as an HTTP/1.1 Upgrade request:

Client Request
GET /chat HTTP/1.1
Host: server.example.com
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
Server Response
HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Accept: s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=

After this handshake, the connection transitions from HTTP to the WebSocket framing protocol.

sections.title: Data Framing
sections.content:
WebSocket uses a lightweight frame-based protocol:

FIN bitIndicates this is the final fragment of a message
Opcode (4 bits)Frame type: 0x1=text, 0x2=binary, 0x8=close, 0x9=ping, 0xA=pong
Mask bitClient-to-server frames must be masked (security measure)
Payload length7 bits, or extended to 16/64 bits for larger messages
Masking key4-byte XOR mask for client frames

sections.title: Use Cases
sections.content:
Chat Applications
Real-time messaging with instant delivery (Slack, Discord)
Live Data Feeds
Stock tickers, sports scores, IoT sensor data
Multiplayer Games
Low-latency game state synchronization
Collaborative Editing
Real-time document collaboration (Google Docs-style)

references.text: Fette, I. and A. Melnikov, "The WebSocket Protocol", RFC 6455, December 2011.
Fielding, R. and J. Reschke, "Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP/1.1)", RFC 7230, June 2014.
